name: Jason Cong
title: Volgenau Chair for Engineering Excellence, Professor
research_summary: Directs the VAST Lab at UCLA, focusing on customizable domain-specific computing, FPGA design automation, and hardware acceleration for machine learning and big-data applications. Pioneer of FPGA high-level synthesis — his tools have been adopted industry-wide and his research has over 43,000 citations.

papers.title: Domain-Specific Computing for Machine Learning: From Chips to Systems
papers.one_line_summary: Explores how building hardware specifically designed for ML tasks — rather than using general-purpose CPUs or GPUs — can achieve orders-of-magnitude improvements in speed and energy efficiency. Covers the full stack from custom silicon chips to system-level design methodologies for deploying these accelerators at scale.

papers.title: FPGA High-Level Synthesis: Past, Present, and Future
papers.one_line_summary: Traces the evolution of high-level synthesis tools that automatically convert C/C++ code into FPGA hardware, from early academic research to widely-used commercial tools like Vivado HLS. Discusses remaining challenges in quality of results, debugging, and making HLS accessible to non-hardware experts.

papers.title: Quantum Computing: An Overview and Progress
papers.one_line_summary: Provides a comprehensive overview of quantum computing fundamentals, current hardware platforms, and the gap between theoretical promise and practical near-term capability. Identifies key research challenges in error correction, qubit scalability, and quantum software that must be solved before quantum advantage becomes widespread.

name: Wei Wang
title: Leonard Kleinrock Chair Professor
research_summary: Directs the Scalable Analytics Institute (ScAI) at UCLA, working at the intersection of machine learning, data mining, and computational biology to extract insights from large-scale biomedical data. Her lab applies NLP and AI to problems in cancer genomics, drug discovery, and clinical medicine, with over 400 publications and fellowships from both ACM and IEEE.

papers.title: Multi-modal Foundation Models for Biological and Clinical Data
papers.one_line_summary: Develops foundation models that jointly learn from diverse biological data types — genomics, proteomics, and clinical records — to enable more accurate disease prediction and drug target identification. Shows that multi-modal pretraining significantly outperforms single-modality models on downstream biomedical tasks.

papers.title: Graph Neural Networks for Knowledge Discovery in Bioinformatics
papers.one_line_summary: Applies graph neural networks to biological knowledge graphs encoding protein interactions, gene pathways, and disease associations to discover novel relationships. Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on drug repurposing and gene function prediction benchmarks.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Clinical NLP and Medical Text Mining
papers.one_line_summary: Investigates how large language models can be fine-tuned on clinical notes and biomedical literature to extract structured medical knowledge automatically. Proposes domain-adaptive pretraining strategies that improve performance on tasks like diagnosis coding and adverse drug event detection.

name: Miryung Kim
title: Professor, Vice Chair of Graduate Studies
research_summary: Focuses on software engineering for data-intensive systems, building debugging, testing, and analysis tools for large-scale platforms like Apache Spark. Her work studies software evolution through code clones and data-driven analytics, and helped define the role of data scientists in software teams, with impact on modern AI-assisted development tools.

papers.title: WhyFlow: Interrogative Debugger for Sensemaking Taint Analysis
papers.one_line_summary: Introduces a debugging system that helps developers understand how data flows through complex programs by allowing them to ask structured 'why' questions, improving reasoning about taint analysis in large-scale systems.

papers.title: Change and Cover: Last-Mile, Pull Request-based Regression Test Augmentation
papers.one_line_summary: Presents a method that uses code changes in pull requests to automatically generate additional regression tests, improving software reliability by targeting uncovered or weakly tested modifications.

papers.title: Fuzzing MLIR Compilers with Custom Mutation Synthesis
papers.one_line_summary: Develops a fuzz testing approach tailored for modern compiler infrastructures like MLIR, generating targeted mutations to uncover bugs in complex compiler pipelines used in machine learning systems.

name: Songwu Lu
title: Professor
research_summary: Leads the WiNG Lab at UCLA, focusing on wireless networking and mobile systems, including 4G/5G cellular networks. His work develops scalable, low-latency, and secure network systems, with contributions to mobile analytics, protocol design, and cloud-assisted wireless infrastructure.

papers.title: MobileInsight: Extracting and Analyzing Cellular Network Information on Smartphones
papers.one_line_summary: Introduces a system that enables fine-grained analysis of cellular network protocols directly on smartphones, providing unprecedented visibility into mobile network performance and behavior.

papers.title: cniCloud: Querying Fine-Grained Cellular Network Information at Scale
papers.one_line_summary: Presents a cloud-based platform that aggregates and queries large-scale cellular network data collected from mobile devices, enabling data-driven insights into network performance and optimization.

papers.title: iCellular: Device-Customized Cellular Network Access on Commodity Smartphones
papers.one_line_summary: Proposes a system that allows smartphones to intelligently select and switch between cellular networks, improving connectivity, performance, and user experience.

name: Todd Millstein
title: Professor
research_summary: Focuses on software reliability using programming languages techniques, with major work in network verification and security. He develops tools like Batfish for analyzing and preventing network failures in large-scale systems used in industry. His research also spans program verification, probabilistic programming, and automated reasoning, aiming to make complex software and network systems more reliable and easier to verify.

papers.title: Tackling Ambiguity in User Intent for LLM-based Network Configuration Synthesis
papers.one_line_summary: Explores how large language models can be used to generate network configurations from natural language while handling ambiguity in user intent to improve correctness and reliability.

papers.title: Tuning Random Generators: Property-Based Testing as Probabilistic Programming
papers.one_line_summary: Connects property-based testing with probabilistic programming by modeling test input generation as a tunable probabilistic process for more effective software testing.

papers.title: Synthesizing Implication Lemmas for Interactive Theorem Proving
papers.one_line_summary: Introduces techniques to automatically generate useful intermediate lemmas to assist users in interactive theorem proving and reduce manual proof effort.

name: Chenchen Ye
title: PhD Student, Scalable Analytics Institute
research_summary: PhD student at UCLA working on machine learning and NLP with a focus on LLM agents for complex real-world tasks such as software engineering. His research explores agentic reasoning, post-training methods, and evaluation of LLM systems, along with integrating heterogeneous knowledge sources such as text, code, graphs, and visual data to improve model robustness and interpretability.

papers.title: Self-Verifying Software Engineering Agents through Discriminative Test Generation
papers.one_line_summary: Proposes LLM-based software engineering agents that improve reliability by generating and using discriminative tests to self-verify outputs and reduce hallucinations in code-related tasks.

papers.title: Training Recipes for Agentic Reinforcement Learning in LLMs: A Survey
papers.one_line_summary: Surveys reinforcement learning approaches for training LLM agents, focusing on techniques that improve planning, reasoning, and decision-making in complex environments.

papers.title: GraphVis: Boosting LLMs with Visual Knowledge Graph Integration
papers.one_line_summary: Introduces a method for integrating visual knowledge graphs into LLM pipelines to improve reasoning and understanding over structured relational data.

name: Serina Chang
title: Assistant Professor
research_summary: Focuses on AI and human behavior, building models that simulate and understand human actions using machine learning and large language models. Her work develops methods for human-AI interaction, behavioral simulation, and data-driven decision-making, with applications in public health, social systems, and policy. She also studies how AI can model populations, infer real-world behaviors from large-scale data, and support high-stakes societal decisions.

papers.title: What do large language models know about opinions?
papers.one_line_summary: Investigates how much LLMs understand human opinions and proposes methods to steer model outputs toward different population perspectives using interpretability techniques.

papers.title: Graph-based alternatives to LLMs for human simulation
papers.one_line_summary: Explores graph-based models as efficient and interpretable alternatives to LLMs for simulating human behavior in structured tasks.

papers.title: ChatBench: from static benchmarks to human-AI evaluation
papers.one_line_summary: Introduces a framework that transforms static benchmarks into interactive human-AI evaluation environments to better measure real-world model performance.
